html:
Said bin Sultan was the ruler of Oman from 1806 to 1856, the height of the Omani Empire. In 1840 he moved his capital from Muscat to Zanzibar.

On Zanzibar he planted cloves on a vast scale, worked by enslaved Africans, and the island became the world's main source of the spice. Zanzibar was also the great slave and ivory market of East Africa, fed by caravans from the interior. He signed trade treaties with Britain, the United States and France.

When he died at sea in 1856, his sons split his lands: one took Muscat and Oman, the other the Sultanate of Zanzibar. Britain made the split final in 1861.
sum: Said bin Sultan was the ruler of Oman from 1806 to 1856, the height of the Omani Empire. In 1840 he moved his capital from Muscat to Zanzibar.
